nodes.name: LMBE synthesis of Sv@MoS2
nodes.procedure: Benefiting by the ultrahigh vacuum environment (pressure in chamber is 1.2 × 10-8 Torr) and the high substrate temperature (600°C), monolayer MoS2 with abundant in situ generated sulfur vacancies (Sv@MoS2) is prepared by laser molecular beam epitaxy (LMBE) as developed before. More specifically, ablate the high-purity MoS2 target (purity 99.99%) by KrF pulse laser (248 nm, 5 Hz) for 3 min, and then the generated MoS2 plasma plumes would deposit on 300 nm SiO2/Si substrate. When MoS2/SiO2/Si sample cooled to room temperature naturally, the Sv@MoS2 was prepared successfully.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Sv@MoS2: Benefiting by the ultrahigh vacuum environment... the Sv@MoS2 was prepared successfully.

nodes.name: LMBE anchoring of Gd SAs
nodes.procedure: On basis of preparation of Sv@MoS2, Gd@MoS2 was further in situ prepared by the same LMBE method. Briefly, considering the sulfur vacancies in Sv@MoS2 as the anchoring sites for Gd SAs, the high-purity Gd target (purity 99.99%) was in situ ablated by KrF pulse laser (248 nm, 5 Hz) for 30 s (or 8 s for low loading), and then the generated Gd plasma plumes would be anchored at the sulfur vacancies of Sv@MoS2/SiO2/Si.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Gd@MoS2: On basis of preparation of Sv@MoS2... anchored at the sulfur vacancies of Sv@MoS2/SiO2/Si.

nodes.name: Layer transfer to glassy carbon
nodes.procedure: For subsequent electrochemical tests, a necessary process to transfer catalyst to glassy carbon was needed. At first, spin-coating of a thin layer of polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA, Alfa Aesar) was done over the catalyst of Gd@MoS2, at a speed of 3000 rpm for 2 min. Then, PMMA/Gd@MoS2 was baked at 120°C for 1 min. After etching the SiO2 layer of SiO2/Si substrate by 2 mol L-1 KOH solution at 95°C, the suspended PMMA/Gd@MoS2 film was picked out and transferred to deionized water to remove a small amount of KOH and etching residues. Pick it up by glassy carbon sheet and dry it naturally. Finally, dissolve the top PMMA layer on Gd@MoS2 with acetone, and then the working electrode was transferred successfully.

nodes.characterization_summary: Numerous bright spots of atomic size with no obvious clusters are evenly dispersed on well-crystallized MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through spherical aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) technique, it is obtained that the numerous bright spots of atomic size with no obvious clusters (Figure 1b) are evenly dispersed on well-crystallized MoS2...

properties.label: e
properties.description: High-resolution microscopy image showing bright spots on dark background with dashed yellow arrow and scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms well-crystallized MoS2 support for Gd@MoS2 catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through spherical aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) technique, it is obtained that the numerous bright spots of atomic size with no obvious clusters (Figure 1b) are evenly dispersed on well-crystallized MoS2 that was confirmed by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) results (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: No Gd-containing crystal phases detected in Gd@MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, by X-ray diffraction (XRD) characterization, it is found that, there are no Gd-containing crystal phases detected in Gd@MoS2 (Figure S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS shows strong intensity at 1220 and 1188 eV corresponding to Gd M4 and Gd M5 edges respectively, confirming bright spots are Gd single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed in Figure 1g, EELS collected from the area marked with red rectangle in Figure 1d shows strong intensity at 1220 and 1188 eV which is corresponds to Gd M4 and Gd M5 edges respectively.

properties.technique: Electron Energy Loss Near Edge Structure (ELNES)

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR signal related to sulfur vacancies decreased largely after Gd SA deposition, indicating atomic anchoring at sulfur vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: More worthwhile to mention that, when Gd SAs were deposited, the signal related with the sulfur vacancies in ESR spectra decreased largely (Figure S2, Supporting Information), denoting that most of Gd element was atomically anchored at the sulfur vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: VSM shows Gd@MoS2 exhibits pronounced M-H in-plane hysteresis loop at 300K and 5K revealing room-temperature in-plane ferromagnetism, while Sv@MoS2 shows unnoticeable hysteresis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results, as depicted in Figure 3a and Figure S5 (Supporting Information), manifest that MoS2 with the anchored Gd atoms exhibit a pronounced M-H in-plane hysteresis loop (at both 300 and 5K) revealing the room-temperature in-plane ferromagnetism and out-of-plane nonmagnetism. In comparison, Sv@MoS2 displays an unnoticeable hysteresis loop...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS spectra of Mo 3d and S 2p show no binding energy shift before and after 22 h AMF-assisted j-t test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectra of Mo 3d and S 2p for Gd@MoS2 before and after the AMF-assisted 22-h j-t test are depicted in Figure 6e,f, and shows no binding energy shift...

nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES measurements since there are no Gd element can be detected in the electrolyte after 22-h j-t test (Figure S16, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: After 22 h AMF-assisted j-t experiment, HAADF-STEM shows no SAs cluster and unnoticeable change in SAs loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image after the long-term stability measurement shows no SAs cluster and unnoticeable change in SAs loading compared to the before one in Figure 1d.
